profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Fidelity Investments | Backend-Focused Full-Stack | Java, Spring Boot, Angular, REST APIs, AWS
profile.summary:
Senior software engineer with 7+ years building production systems at Fidelity Investments. Backend-leaning full-stack — Java, Spring Boot, Angular, and REST APIs powering client-facing financial platforms used by advisors and individual investors.
 
Recent work:
 
Currently leading the modernization of external client-facing investment platforms onto a decoupled Angular + Spring Boot REST API architecture, replacing legacy stacks that had outgrown their original scope. Earlier, built and operated Fidelity's internal observability platform on Prometheus, Grafana, and ELK — serving 2,000+ engineers and 50+ business-critical applications — and modernized its onboarding pipeline to cut time from ~1 day to ~10 minutes.
 
I care about the parts of engineering that compound over time: testing infrastructure that catches problems before production, API contracts that let teams ship in parallel, and automation that removes repetitive work. Recently introduced GitHub Copilot agents into our team workflow to handle version upgrades and PR review, freeing engineers for higher-judgment work.
 
Outside of Fidelity:
 
I build side projects to stay close to the craft. Most recently shipped cricverse.co — a cricket fantasy league platform with a real-time WebSocket auction engine, custom fuzzy player-name matching, and an async FastAPI backend. Built end-to-end in 3 weeks; 50+ users across 10+ private leagues.
 
What I'm interested in:
 
Senior IC engineering roles working on systems with real users, real scale, and real consequences — particularly around backend infrastructure, developer platforms, or product engineering at companies that take engineering quality seriously.
 
Always open to a conversation. Reach me at satyamptl0507@gmail.com.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Leading the modernization of external client-facing investment platforms used by advisors and individual investors, migrating legacy stacks to a decoupled Angular + Java/Spring Boot REST API architecture.
- Led the modernization of external client-facing investment platforms — used by advisors and clients — migrating legacy stacks to a decoupled Angular + Java/Spring Boot REST API architecture.
- Reduced content publishing latency from 2 hours to 20 minutes by re-architecting the distribution pipeline with Java RESTful APIs and event-driven processing, accelerating time-to-market for client-facing financial content.
- Drove architecture and API contract reviews across upstream and downstream teams, defining REST API specifications and integration patterns that enable parallel development and prevent breaking changes during the migration.
- Led team-wide SonarQube adoption that raised code coverage from 27% to 90%+, establishing testing standards and shifting defect detection from post-release to pre-merge across all core services.
- Introduced GitHub Copilot agents and AI-powered automation into the team workflow to handle version upgrades, PR review, and technical documentation generation, reducing review cycle time and offloading repetitive maintenance work.

positions.title: Senior Cloud Engineer
positions.description:
- Owned the internal observability platform serving Fidelity engineering.
- Built and operated an internal observability platform (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK) serving 2,000+ engineers and 50+ business-critical applications across Fidelity, enabling proactive alerting that reduced mean time to detection and accelerated incident resolution for revenue-impacting services.
- Modernized the platform onboarding pipeline by replacing a legacy nightly batch job with FastAPI services and Ansible automation, reducing application onboarding time from ~1 day to ~10 minutes (~99% reduction).
- Designed self-service tooling in Python and Java that allowed teams to autonomously onboard log analysis, exporter metrics, and health checks, eliminating a recurring support bottleneck.
